apple-a.adjustment: -0.3: centred dark serif hero is the closest thing here to the 'plain' pages the founder rejected, and it moves the brand punchline down to the footer CTA
apple-a.best: The clearest demo of Sharpen in the set: a huge soft line gets amber squiggles, the Sharpen pill presses, the sharp line lands with a 'Cut the warm-up' receipt and Kept chips. It cycles all four real examples, and the whole before/after/receipt fits in the first phone viewport.
apple-a.worst: Calm, centred and Apple-polite. 'Same idea. Sharper line.' is clear but has less bite than 'Good ideas die in bad first lines.', which it pushes to the footer. The 1440 hero reads as a nicer version of the current page, not a new one.

apple-b.best: The loudest hero in the set: a full-bleed ultramarine field, huge 'Write the line they stop for.', and the one crisp post standing still in a blurred feed of soft openers. The terse headings land ('Soft in. Sharp out.', '11 PM idea. 8:40 AM post.', 'Start at $0. No card.').
apple-b.worst: The hero never shows the edit happen. The old line is a 12px strikethrough above a static card, so the product only explains itself after a scroll. Inter replaces Newsreader and the light sections drift from the app. 'They stop for' leans towards an outcome promise.

linear-a.adjustment: -0.4: centred headline over a 3-pane app screenshot is exactly Typefully's homepage structure, which the founder ruled out
linear-a.best: Most buildable: the hero is the real composer (sidebar, word-level diff, live X preview, Sharpen/Undo). 'Bring the idea. Leave with the hook.' is a strong closer, and the X payout table ('the bar, as of Oct 2026') is the most honest framing of those numbers.
linear-a.worst: The edit happens at about 22px inside a screenshot, so nobody sees it in one second. Structurally this is the current homepage plus Typefully's screenshot-under-headline, the opposite of 'not plain, not a clone'.

linear-b.adjustment: -0.2: below the hero it is monochrome dark sections that a founder who already called the pages 'plain' may read as plain again
linear-b.best: Best copy and best explanation of the move. 'Your idea is fine. / Your first line isn't.' is the sharpest headline across all ten, and the type-specimen hero labels every edit on the real line (CUT The warm-up, CUT The hedge, MOVE Asked it as a question, KEPT Your facts) across four switchable examples.
linear-b.worst: On desktop the H1 sits under the specimen (y≈674), so the first thing a visitor sees is an annotated quote with no product name. It drops ultramarine for a bone pill, so the brand breaks at the signup handoff. 'Four beats, about two seconds' is an unverified speed claim.

awwwards-a.adjustment: -0.2: the hero card visibly scrambles mid-transition ('Most underrated thing in / trading? Sizing / after' stacked, 'myfirst' collisions)
awwwards-a.best: 'Features worded to pop', done literally: every feature title is a sharpened line with the generic SaaS version struck beneath it ('we show you previews for every platform' becomes 'Four feeds. One draft.'). The page demonstrates the product on itself.
awwwards-a.worst: The cutting floor is a pile of loose words at the fold that overlap and read as noise, worse at 390. The lede sits about 180px below the headline with dead space. The hero shows only the result, never the soft line next to it.

awwwards-b.best: 'Write it rough. Post it sharp.' is the clearest plain-English promise in the set, and 'Your facts stay. The fluff goes.' and 'Bring it rough. We'll sharpen it.' follow it well. The taped galley proof with blue-pencil marks and a handwritten 'Led with the question.' is charming and crafted.
awwwards-b.worst: The proofs are monospace with carets and loops on top, so they read as hard work, especially the churn example and at 390, where the sharp line falls below the fold. Four typefaces, all-caps mono buttons and a light paper theme make it the second-costliest rebrand. Mono kicker labels sit above the who-for h3s (a rule hit).

typefully-a.best: 'They read one line. / Make it hookworthy.' uses the brand name as the payoff. The hero tells the whole story: squiggled draft, then the sharpened X post, then a receipt naming the move. 'See the squiggle? Tap Sharpen.' teaches the product in five words, and the playground flags soft words in your own line, honestly ('the rewrite runs in the app').
typefully-a.worst: The three-card stack is busy, and the receipt, the one thing nobody else has, is cut at the 1440x900 fold and lands below the fold on phones. The final 'Yours won't.' is a soft promise. The network chips fail AA (4.33:1 at 11.5px).

typefully-b.best: The thermal receipt hanging from the nav rule (YOUR LINE, CUT, KEPT, MOVE 'Led with the number', Voice 'still yours') is the most ownable proof object here. 'Every edit, on the record.', 'Nothing posts until you do.', pricing printed as receipts and a final input that underlines your own soft words all fit one idea.
typefully-b.worst: The hero is static, and the receipt is dense mono you have to read, so it fails the one-second test as a picture. On a 390 phone the receipt drops below the fold, leaving the headline and chips. Paper, EB Garamond and Caveat put it off the app's brand.

arc-a.best: The most impactful in-brand answer to 'plain': the punchline on a full ultramarine stage (#2B52FF, white text passes AA), amber stickers on 'so i think the' and 'is honestly just', an @heycape cursor taps Sharpen, the stickers peel into a 'Peeled off' tray, and side cards show 0 soft spots and fits X/Threads/LinkedIn/Bluesky.
arc-a.worst: Below the hero it drops back to standard dark SaaS with generic headings ('Then everything after the first line'). 'Start free. Pay when it works.' implies pay-on-results. Mid-peel the stickers float over the words, the receipt sits below the 900px fold, and it flashes at load before the peel.

arc-b.best: The best one-second poster in the set, and the least like Typefully. Heavy grotesk 'Good ideas die' over an italic serif 'in bad first lines.' does the before→after in type alone. The proof card strikes the soft words and highlights the real rewrite in lime, a receipt peeks below, and 'Try yours' underlines your own soft words honestly. The pastel receipt cards for all four examples are great proof.
arc-b.worst: A full rebrand: lime and paper, Bricolage and Instrument Serif, about 300KB of inlined fonts, against a dark ultramarine Newsreader app, so signup lands somewhere that looks like a different product. The hero is static, it shares the arc-a copy including 'Pay when it works', and the mobile page is the longest (≈14.7k px).

top5.why: This is the only concept that fixes 'plain' without leaving the brand. The blue stage plus a hands-on sticker peel on heycape's real line grabs in one second and needs no new tokens or fonts, so it drops straight into the app's system. Proof is strong (peel, Peeled-off tray, four rewrite rows with highlighted soft words and named moves); copy below the hero is its weakest part and is easy to fix by borrowing lines.

'They read one line. Make it hookworthy.' is the best in-brand H1 after the punchline itself, and the hero shows the whole value chain (squiggled draft, sharp post, receipt) with no screenshot chrome. 'See the squiggle? Tap Sharpen.' and an honest type-your-own playground make it the most conversion-literate page; it needs the stack tidied so the receipt is above the fold.

Best clarity and proof per pixel: the edit happens at display size, with a receipt and Kept chips, and it all fits the first phone viewport. It is also perfectly consistent and cheap to build. It ranks below the top two only because it looks closest to the 'plain' pages the founder rejected and hides the brand punchline.

The strongest raw hero of the ten. The two-voice type (heavy and sharp, then italic and soft), the lime highlight on the rewrite and the receipt make the before→after visible before anyone reads, and it is the furthest from Typefully. As a whole it costs a full rebrand of a live app, so its value is as a source of the hero composition and receipt cards, not as the page to ship.

It has the best headline ('Your idea is fine. Your first line isn't.') and the best explanation of what Sharpen did (leader-line labels for cut, move and kept on the real sentence). The desktop H1 sits under the specimen and blue is dropped, so as built it loses clarity and fit, but its copy and specimen labels should go into the winner.

steal: awwwards-a: under each sharpened feature title, strike the generic SaaS line beneath it ('we show you previews for every platform' becomes 'Four feeds. One draft.'). It makes the features pop and shows Sharpen on the page itself.
awwwards-b: 'Write it rough. Post it sharp.' (best plain promise; use it as the hero sub-line or Sharpen H2), 'Your facts stay. The fluff goes.', and the closer 'Bring it rough. We'll sharpen it.'

apple-b: put the blurred feed of soft-opening posts (deltaneutral 'genuinely curious what you all think about', 'honestly not sure if this will resonate') behind the one sharp card on arc-a's blue stage. It shows why the first line matters before anyone reads.
apple-b: 'Soft in. Sharp out.' as the Sharpen H2, 'Start at $0. No card.' as the pricing H2, and the '309 / 280: on free X it becomes a thread of 2' counter for Previews.

typefully-b: use the thermal receipt (YOUR LINE / CUT / KEPT / MOVE / Words 18 → 9 / Voice 'still yours') as the receipt object everywhere, add 'Every edit, on the record.' and 'Nothing posts until you do.', and end on a live-underline input ('Your next post starts here.') instead of a plain CTA band.

linear-a: 'Bring the idea. Leave with the hook.' as the final CTA, and the X payout table framing ('X creator payouts, the bar as of Oct 2026, Original posts count / Replies don't') in place of giant 'Premium 500 500K' numerals that a skimmer can mistake for Hookworthy stats.

linear-b (top 5, but worth folding into arc-a): 'Your idea is fine. Your first line isn't.' as the Sharpen section H2, the CUT/MOVE/KEPT leader labels on the hero line, the strip '90 → 59 chars · Fits X, Threads, LinkedIn, Bluesky · Facts kept', and the 'You type. It flags. You tap. It explains.' four-beat demo.
notes: Hygiene: all ten pass the automated checks (no horizontal scroll at 360/390/1440, no h1/h2 over 2 lines, no banned words, no console errors). Prices are exact, including the monthly toggle ($16 and $24 appear in every concept; Free shows 20 rewrites + 50 touch-ups and 15 auto-posts; Pro shows 250 + 1,750 and 500 auto-posts; Studio shows 500 per client voice). Every 'try your own' (arc-b, typefully-a, typefully-b) only flags soft words and says the rewrite runs in the app, which is honest. Minor rule hits: typefully-a network chips 4.33:1 at 11.5px; awwwards-b black X preview label 2.79:1; awwwards-b mono kicker labels above the who-for h3s; linear-b who-for h3s include a sub-label (3 lines); linear-b 'Four beats, about two seconds'; typefully-a 'Yours won't.'; arc-a/arc-b 'Pay when it works' (reads as pay-on-results; it is a subscription). Linear-a's 1.00:1 contrast flags are opacity-0 animation states, not real failures. Cross-cutting conversion problems: (1) No hero says who it is for or where it posts. Every sub is some version of 'Hookworthy sharpens yours in one tap. It still sounds like you.', and only the proof chrome hints at X/Threads/LinkedIn/Bluesky. The winner should put the networks into the proof line (linear-b/arc-a's 'Fits X, Threads, LinkedIn, Bluesky' strip) or the sub. (2) The copy has converged: 8/10 share 'Traders first. Anyone with a take.', 'It drafts. You press send.' and 'Replies don't pay. Posts do.', so the winner needs its own lines (see steal). (3) apple-a, apple-b, typefully-a and awwwards set X's bar as giant numerals ('Premium / 500 / 500K'). A skimmer reads those as product stats; use a labelled table or a sentence. (4) Every page runs 11–15k px on a phone; cut the who-for and 'everything after the first line' blocks by a third. Recommendation: build on arc-a's hero (in brand, high impact), use typefully-a's H1 or linear-b's line as the Sharpen H2, adopt typefully-b's receipt object and awwwards-a's struck-generic feature titles, and borrow apple-a's display-size before→after for phone.
